description:
This dataset (L2PSCMaskAux) contains auxiliary information for the Cloud-Aerosol Lidar and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observation (CALIPSO) Lidar Level 2 Polar Stratospheric Cloud (PSC) Product (L2PSCMask) that are derived from the Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS) H2O and HNO3 products and the Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) temperatures. The L2PSCMaskAux product covers the time period 1 May 2008 to 12 September 2018 during which the CALIPSO/CALIOP and Aura/MLS orbit tracks were closely maintained within the Afternoon Satellite Constellation (A-Train) to better than 20 km and 60 seconds. The L2PSCMaskAux files contain a 30 minute partial orbit with a spatial coverage over the polar winter cap with a lower latitude of 28° N for the Arctic winter and 28° S for the Antarctic winter. The temporal resolution of the profile data is approximately 25 seconds corresponding to a distance of 168 km along track. A number of parameters related to the air parcel temperature histories at each of the collocated CALIOP/MLS measurement locations are included in the auxiliary dataset. The temperature histories are derived from the Aura MLS Lagrangian Trajectory Diagnostics (LTDs), developed under the NASA Aura Science Team program (Livesey et al, 2015). The LTDs describe motion along diabatic air parcel trajectories computed using NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) winds and temperature tendencies, spanning 15 days prior to and 15 days following each MLS observation. 

Following Lambert et al. (2012), we quantify the duration of exposure of an air parcel to low temperatures by defining the temperature threshold exposure (TTE) as the total integrated time that the air parcel is subjected to synoptic-scale temperatures below a particular threshold. The temperature history is computed following the diabatic back-trajectory for up to 15 days, with TTE defined as the total time (in days) that an air parcel remains continuously below TICE + 4 K, where TICE is the ice frost point at t = 0. Other temperature parameters include the minimum temperature encountered along the back trajectory and the temperature change over the last day along the back trajectory. 

References Lambert, A., Santee, M. L., Wu, D. L., and Chae, J. H.: A-train CALIOP and MLS observations of early winter Antarctic polar stratospheric clouds and nitric acid in 2008, Atmos. Chem. Phys., 12, 2899–2931, https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-12-2899-2012, 2012. Livesey, N. J., Santee, M. L., and Manney, G. L.: A Match-based approach to the estimation of polar stratospheric ozone loss using Aura Microwave Limb Sounder observations, Atmos. Chem. Phys., 15, 9945–9963, https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-15-9945-2015, 2015.
title: CALIPSO Lidar Level 2 Polar Stratospheric Cloud (PSC) Auxiliary, V1-00
